A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same MLLM4PUE/PMEB study, with reliably matchable methods, equations, experiments and displays. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF includes an appendix or the separately referenced supplementary materials.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, classification and composed-retrieval experiments, plus prompt and embedding-fusion ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds classification comparisons, modality-gap measurements and sample-size analyses.

M1.justification: The summarization prompts, last-token embeddings, contrastive objective, QLoRA adaptation and zero-shot procedures remain substantively unchanged. v2's explicit LoRA discussion and 8B backbone designation expand documentation rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds Databiox classification with 922 images in Tables 1 and 3, increasing classification coverage from 12 to 13 tasks. The other evaluation datasets, three task families and training corpora are retained; changes to existing sample counts concern protocol rather than new coverage.

E2.justification: CONCH becomes an evaluated classification comparator in v2 Table 3; v1 discussed it but omitted it from that comparison. PLIP, PathCLIP, QuiltNet and E5-V remain, and the retrieval comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 replaces CONCH-ranked selection of 500 high-scoring, 500 low-scoring and 500 random images with 1,000 category-preserving random samples for large datasets, except Osteo. v2 adds classification accuracy, modality-gap evaluation and comparisons using 1,000, 3,000, 5,000 and all samples. Table 1 also revises Wsss4luad's reported source size from 4,693 to 10,091.

E4.justification: v2 adds t-SNE and quantitative modality-gap analysis in Section 5.4/Figure 4, and benchmark sample-size sensitivity in Section 5.5/Figure 5. v1's prompt and prompt-tuning ablation in Section 5.4.1/Table 4 is absent from the supplied v2. The embedding-fusion ablation remains in Table 5.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports 100 classification trials drawing from 21 templates and displays distributions, medians and quartiles in Figure 4. v2 replaces these with point scores in Table 3 without reporting trial counts, variability or aggregation. This substantially changes statistical reporting, but does not establish that fewer trials were actually performed.

E6.justification: v2 replaces classification distributions with a wF1/accuracy table, adds Databiox and CONCH results, and reports new sample-size and alignment findings. For example, Arch-PubMed modality gaps are 0.9284 for PathCLIP and 0.2587 for MLLM4PUE-P. Prompt-ablation results disappear. Classification changes cannot be interpreted as same-setting gains; retrieval, composed-retrieval and fusion-ablation numerical tables are unchanged after matching renumbering.

T1.justification: The embedding construction and contrastive-loss equation remain unchanged, with no added assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations. The new modality-gap analysis applies a cited empirical metric without developing new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the introductory and Figure 1 performance claim from superiority across all tasks to most tasks, while retaining the central framework and benchmark contributions. Its abstract expands PMEB from 15 tasks/14 datasets to 16/15, although Section 3.1 and Table 1's caption retain the old counts.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive arguments that reduced modality gaps demonstrate better alignment, sample-size stability validates the smaller benchmark, and question-only comparisons validate multimodal requirements. It also attributes CONCH's advantages to larger training data and emphasizes data efficiency. These broaden the interpretation substantially, while the earlier prompt-effect interpretation disappears.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies PyTorch, LLaVA-NeXT-8B, an accumulated batch size of 144 and learning rate of 4e-4. It also clarifies composed-retrieval input handling for E5-V and CLIP-based comparators. These extend previously documented implementation details without establishing changes to the underlying training settings.

R1.justification: v2 strengthens its differentiation from E5-V by contrasting LoRA adaptation on existing image-text pairs with claimed pathology-instruction pretraining requirements. It adds Liang et al.'s modality-gap work and removes two background references on hierarchical vision transformers and mutation heterogeneity. The central positioning against separate-encoder pathology models remains.

P1.justification: The title, author list, abstract, introduction and conclusion receive edits. Related-work topics are reversed, and numbered experimental subsections become named paragraphs. These are localized narrative and organizational revisions within the same overall structure; much of the method exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the classification boxplots with a substantial two-metric table, removes the prompt-ablation table, and adds modality-gap and sample-size figures. The radar chart gains Databiox and revised styling, comparison tables gain training-dataset color groups, and existing method displays are relocated. These substantially change how the evidence is presented.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence through CONCH comparisons, sample-size checks, modality-gap analysis and additional implementation details. However, it removes the direct prompt-strategy ablation and 100-trial template-variability reporting, leaves classification aggregation unspecified, and introduces inconsistent benchmark counts. These gains and losses affect important aspects of evidential strength, so the supplied PDFs do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
